title.narrative: Institutional strengthening Interamerican court of human rights
Institutionellt stärkande Interamerikanska domstolen för mänskliga rättigheter

description.narrative:
The objective of the intervention is to contribute to the institutional strengthening of the Inter American Court of Human Rights in order to improve the human rights situation in the States Parties to the American Convention of Human Rights.
The objective will be achieve through 4 main outcomes:
1. Strengthen the jurisdictional activity of the Inter-American Court by supporting the holding of sessions and the conduct of judicial proceedings in the States.
2. Strengthen the resources and computer security of the Inter-American Court and its Library.
3. Strengthen the human rights training capacities of the Inter-American Court.
4. Strengthen the dissemination of the work and jurisprudence of the Inter-American Court through the translation of key decisions.

Insatsen löper över tre år, 2023-2025, med ett totalt belopp på 24 000 000 kr, och omfattar:
1) Stöd till domstolens rättegångsarbete under sessionsperioderna, samt till rättsliga förfaranden på plats i medlemsländerna.
2) Förstärkning av informationshanteringen, inklusive informationssäkerhet, samt stöd till domstolens virtuella bibliotek.
3) Förstärkning av domstolens kursverksamhet
4) Stöd till arbetet med att informera om domstolens rättspraxis, inklusive översättning av domar till engelska och portugisiska.

The support covers three years, 2023-2025, with a total amount of SEK 24 000 000, and aims at continuing the lines of work previously supported by Sweden, including:
1) Strengthening of the jurisdictional work of the Court by supporting the periods of sessions and carrying out legal proceedings in the member states.
2) Strengthening of information management including security of information and the resources of the Court and its library.
3) Strengthening of the training capacities of the Court.
4) Strengthening the work with dissemination of Court jurisprudence, including translation of key decisions.

title.narrative: Agreement Inter American Court for Human Rights
Agreement, Inter American Court of Human Rights 2023 - 2025
Decision Inter American Court for Human Rights

description.narrative:
In 2024, the Inter-American Court of Human Rights made significant progress in strengthening its judicial work, technological capacity, training programs, and dissemination of jurisprudence. With the support of Sweden and the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida), the Court advanced its mandate to protect human rights and promote access to justice across the Americas.
Main Achievements of outcome 1: Strengthen Jurisdictional Activity.
A. Sessions
Throughout 2024, the Court held eight periods of sessions, totaling 23 weeks of deliberations. Ten weeks were conducted in person and 13 virtually. The Court successfully carried out 21 of the 23 planned weeks surpassing the original target of 19 weeks.
In terms of key jurisprudential advances, in 2024, the Court issued a series of judgments that consolidated important legal standards in the Inter-American system. Among the major developments:
-The duty to prevent human rights violations in counter-terrorism contexts (AMIA v. Argentina) Collective life project and equality in land titling for communities facing structural racial discrimination (Quilombola Communities of Alcântara v. Brazil) -Protection of women searching for disappeared relatives, even from exile (Ubaté and Bogotá v. Colombia) -Prohibition of automatic pretrial detention (Reyes Mantilla v. Ecuador) -Limits on military jurisdiction over retired personnel (Poggioli v. Venezuela) -State obligations regarding racial discrimination in public and private spheres (Dos Santos Nascimento and Ferreira Gomes v. Brazil) -Duty to ensure electoral integrity and genuine elections (Capriles v. Venezuela) -Recognition of the right to education under Article 26 of the American Convention (SENAME v. Chile) -Recognition of the right to housing (Quilombola Communities of Alcântara v. Brazil) -Right of Indigenous Peoples to remain in voluntary isolation (Tagaeri and Taromenane v. Ecuador)
These developments reinforce democratic integrity, reduce arbitrariness, strengthen social rights protections, and advance equality and inclusion in the region.
B. Judicial Proceedings and On-Site Visits
An important innovation in this project phase was support for judicial proceedings conducted directly in Member States, both before and after judgments. Examples include:
-New compliance monitoring mechanism (approved Oct. 8, 2024) allowing working meetings with States to clarify reparations, deadlines, compliance requests, and objections. -Visit to Guatemala (Oct. 2829, 2024) to review 35 pending judgments and six provisional measures concerning issues such as access to justice, death penalty, violence against women and children, Indigenous rights, and protection of human rights defenders. -Monitored guarantees include legislative reforms, gender-based violence prevention mechanisms, reforms to forensic institutions, specialized courts for femicide, and translation of the American Convention into the Achi Mayan language.
Main Achievements of outcome 2: Strengthen the resources and computer security.
Software Renewal
In 2024, the Court renewed several critical software licenses. These updates were essential to ensure the security and efficiency of institutional operations in a context of increasing reliance on digital and cloud based tools.
Enhancing Information and Knowledge Management
Key actions included:
-Improved jurisprudence search tools -Renewal of specialized legal database licenses -Acquisition of new physical and digital resources -Expanded accessibility features for persons with disabilities
These measures have enhanced case processing efficiency and access to legal information. Verification documents for these improvements are available at the Courts Secretariat and in Annex III of the 2024 Annual Narrative Report.
Web Accessibility
The Court advanced its accessibility initiative, enabling individuals with physical and cognitive disabilities to more easily use Library services through enhanced digital tools.
Main Achievements of outcome 3: Information and knowledge management
In 2024, the Court developed three new selfpaced online courses (in Spanish) on:
-Conventionality Control -Political Rights -Judicial Independence
Launched on December 20, these courses reached 119 enrollments within six days, bringing total enrollments from 20232024 to 1,305 participants. With six of nine planned courses completed, the Courts Training Center continues to expand access to highquality human rights education for States Parties and the general public.
Main Achievements of outcome 4: Translation of key decisions
The Court translated 14 judgments into English and two into Portuguese, covering a broad range of regional human rights issues.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
